verses.text: This is the LORD's message that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the nations.

About Egypt: This is about the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was at Carchemish by the Euphrates River. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated it in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
"Get your shields ready, large and small, and march out to battle!
Harness the horses! Mount up, you riders! Take your places with your helmets on! Sharpen your spears! Put on your armor!
But what do I see? They are terrified and running away. Their soldiers are defeated. They run in a hurry and do not look back. There is terror on every side," says the LORD.
"The fastest cannot run away, and the strongest cannot escape. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.
Who is this rising like the Nile, like rivers with surging waters?
Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers with surging waters. Egypt says, 'I will rise and cover the earth. I will destroy cities and the people in them.'
Charge, you horses! Race wildly, you chariots! Let the soldiers march out: men from Cush and Put who carry shields, and men from Lud who use the bow.

But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies. It is a day of revenge, when he will pay back his enemies. The sword will eat until it is full and drink their blood until it is satisfied. For the Lord GOD of Armies will offer a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get healing balm, young woman of Egypt. You try many medicines, but they do no good. There is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame. Your cries fill the earth. One soldier stumbles over another, and they both fall down together."
This is the message the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon coming to attack Egypt:
"Announce it in Egypt. Proclaim it in Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes: 'Take your positions and get ready, because the sword is devouring everything around you.'
Why have your strong soldiers been swept away? They cannot stand, because the LORD has pushed them down.
He makes many stumble. They fall over one another. They say, 'Get up! Let us go back to our own people, to the land where we were born, away from the cruel sword.'
There they shout, 'Pharaoh king of Egypt is nothing but noise. He has missed his chance.'
As surely as I live," says the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies, "someone is coming who is like Mount Tabor among the mountains, like Mount Carmel by the sea.
Pack your bags for exile, you people living in Egypt. For Memphis will become a ruin, burned down, with no one living there.
Egypt is a beautiful young cow, but a horsefly is coming from the north to attack her. It is coming.

Even the hired soldiers in her army are like fattened calves. They too will turn and run away together. They will not stand their ground, because the day of disaster is coming on them, the time for them to be punished.
Egypt will hiss like a snake slithering away as the enemy army marches in. They will come against her with axes, like men cutting down trees.
They will cut down her forest," says the LORD, "even though it is so thick no one can get through it. They are more numerous than locusts. No one can count them.
The people of Egypt will be put to shame. They will be handed over to the people of the north."
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I am going to punish Amon, the god of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and her kings, Pharaoh and all who trust in him.
I will hand them over to those who want to kill them, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But later Egypt will be lived in again, as in the past," says the LORD.

"But do not be afraid, Jacob my servant. Do not be discouraged, Israel. For look, I will rescue you from far away, and your descendants from the land where they are captives. Jacob will come back and have peace and quiet. No one will make him afraid.

Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant," says the LORD, "for I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will correct you fairly, but I will not let you go unpunished."
